title: Titanium Embolization Coil Mandrel
alloyReason: Nitinol (ASTM F2063) is specified for this interventional self-expanding application where 55-60Ni wt% delivers superelastic recovery up to 8% at body temp. Af temperature is set 10-15C below operating temp for complete austenitic transformation. This rationale is driven by embolization coil delivery mandrel (nitinol) and specific design requirements.
process: CNC swiss turning for interventional geometry
Ultrasonic clean Class 10k at 200W fiber laser
surfaceTreatment: Electropolishing + passivation per ASTM F86 (20-30% HNO3, 30min @50C) achieving Ra <0.2um for implant-grade finish — tailored for embolization coil delivery application
commonFailures: Galvanic pitting at Ti-316L interface in vivo - eliminated by ceramic Al2O3 coating on mating surfaces — critical for embolization coil delivery performance

faq.q: What specific material properties make Titanium Embolization Coil Mandrel suitable for Embolization coil delivery mandrel (Nitinol)?
faq.a: Titanium Embolization Coil Mandrel uses Nitinol because its yield strength, fatigue endurance, and corrosion resistance directly address interventional operational demands. The alloy's specific strength enables mass reduction without section compromise, while the TiO2 passivation ensures long-term environmental resistance.

faq.q: What are the critical dimensional tolerances for Titanium Embolization Coil Mandrel?
faq.a: Standard machining tolerance for Titanium Embolization Coil Mandrel is +/-0.05mm (ISO 2768-m). Functional mating surfaces are held to +/-0.025mm with Ra 0.8um finish, verified specifically for embolization coil delivery requirements. Threaded features conform to ISO 965-2 Class 6g, verified with calibrated Go/No-Go ring gauges on 100% of production.

faq.q: Does Titanium Embolization Coil Mandrel require any post-machining surface treatment?
faq.a: Yes. embolization coil delivery components require Electropolishing + passivation per ASTM F86 (20-30% HNO3, 30min @50C) achieving Ra <0.2um for implant-grade finish — tailored for embolization coil delivery application. This restores the natural TiO2 passive layer removed during machining and provides the required surface properties for the specific service environment. Key parameters include surface finish Ra 0.8um and passive layer thickness verification per applicable standards.

faq.q: What quality documentation is included with Titanium Embolization Coil Mandrel shipments?
faq.a: Each shipment of Titanium Embolization Coil Mandrel includes: (1) EN 10204 Type 3.1 MTR with full chemical analysis and mechanical properties; (2) Certificate of Conformance confirming all processes meet embolization coil delivery specifications; (3) Dimensional inspection report with actual vs nominal measurements on critical features; (4) Surface roughness certification per applicable standards. FAIR available on request.

faq.q: What is the MOQ and typical lead time for Coil pusher / Embolization wire interventional components?
faq.a: Standard MOQ: 1 unit for prototype evaluation. Production lead time: 15-25 business days depending on quantity. Rush orders (3-5 days) available. Contact our supply chain team for volume-based tiered pricing.
